## Comparability caveat

The two years are **not directly comparable on an as-originally-reported basis**. On November 3, 2021, IBM separated its managed infrastructure services unit into Kyndryl Holdings, and "the historical results of Kyndryl have been presented as discontinued operations in these consolidated financial statements" [ibm_fy2022_notes.txt]. As a result, FY2020 revenue appears two different ways:

- **As originally reported** in the FY2020 10-K (including the managed infrastructure business): **$73,620 million** [ibm_fy2020_10k.txt]
- **As recast for continuing operations** in the FY2022 10-K: **$55,179 million** [ibm_fy2022_income_statement.txt]

FY2022 revenue was **$60,530 million**, which reflects continuing operations only (post-Kyndryl) [ibm_fy2022_income_statement.txt].

## Calculation

| Basis | FY2020 | FY2022 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Like-for-like (continuing ops, both years) | $55,179M | $60,530M | **+$5,351M, +9.7%** |
| As-reported headline (not comparable) | $73,620M | $60,530M | –$13,090M, –17.8% |

The **+9.7%** figure is the economically meaningful answer, since it compares the same set of businesses in both periods. The –17.8% headline decline is almost entirely an artifact of the Kyndryl spinoff removing the managed infrastructure services revenue, not an organic contraction.

ANSWER: On a comparable continuing-operations basis, IBM revenue grew ~9.7% from FY2020 ($55,179M) to FY2022 ($60,530M). (On an as-originally-reported basis FY2020 revenue was $73,620M, implying a 17.8% decline, but that comparison is distorted by the November 2021 Kyndryl spinoff being reclassified to discontinued operations.)
